extra.message: SQL injection in Student.create(): the user-supplied name is interpolated into the SQL query with Python %-formatting ("VALUES ('%(name)s')" % {'name': name}) and executed without parameterization. name originates from POST /students/ form field data['name'] (sqli/views.py:57) with no sanitization, so an attacker can inject arbitrary SQL (e.g., a name containing ' + SQL payload) to read, modify, or delete the entire database.

The courses() view handler creates courses on POST /courses/ without any authentication or authorization check (no @authorize decorator, no get_auth_user call). The UI (sqli/templates/courses.jinja2) restricts the create-course form to authenticated admins ({% if auth_user and auth_user.is_admin %}), but the server-side handler does not enforce this. Any unauthenticated user can create arbitrary courses, bypassing the intended admin-only privilege.

The evaluate() view handler creates marks on POST /students/{student_id}/evaluate/{course_id} without any authentication or admin check (no @authorize decorator). The UI (sqli/templates/course.jinja2) only shows the evaluate form to admins ({% if auth_user.is_admin %}), but the server-side handler allows any unauthenticated user to submit grades for any student and course, bypassing the intended admin-only privilege.

The students() view handler creates students on POST /students/ without any authentication check (no @authorize decorator, no get_auth_user call). The UI (sqli/templates/students.jinja2) only shows the add-student form to authenticated users ({% if auth_user %}), but the server-side handler does not enforce this, so any unauthenticated user can create students.

Users can inject scripts via POST /students/, POST /courses/, and POST /courses/{id}/review which are then rendered unescaped in students.jinja2:16, courses.jinja2:17-18, course.jinja2:14-15,22, and student.jinja2:19-20.

extra.message: CSRF protection is disabled: csrf_middleware is commented out (# csrf_middleware) in the application middleware list, although a working implementation exists in sqli/middlewares.py:26-38. Templates include _csrf_token fields but they are never validated. All state-changing POST endpoints (login, student creation, course creation, review creation, evaluation, logout) are vulnerable to cross-site request forgery, allowing an attacker to perform authenticated actions on behalf of a logged-in user via a malicious third-party page.

Session storage is created with httponly=False, so the session cookie is accessible to JavaScript via document.cookie. Combined with the stored XSS vulnerabilities and the disabled CSRF middleware, an attacker can read the victim's session cookie and hijack their authenticated session.

Passwords are checked with an unsalted MD5 hash comparison (pwd_hash == md5(password).hexdigest()). MD5 is a fast, cryptographically broken hash unsuitable for password storage, enabling efficient rainbow-table and brute-force attacks against leaked pwd_hash values. Seed data (migrations/001-fixtures.sql) also stores MD5 hashes, including a default admin account superadmin with password 'superadmin'.

cwe: CWE-327: Use of a Broken or Risky Cryptographic Algorithm

extra.message: On successful login the existing session is reused without rotating the session identifier: session['user_id'] = user.id is set on the pre-authentication session (created on any prior page view, e.g., session['last_visited'] at sqli/views.py:29). An attacker who can plant or learn the victim's pre-login session cookie (feasible via the stored XSS or same-site subdomains) gains a valid authenticated session after the victim logs in.

The aiohttp application is created with debug=True. Debug mode is not intended for production: it enables verbose error output and internal state in logs when handling requests, risking disclosure of sensitive information such as stack traces and configuration details.

Fixture data seeds user accounts with hardcoded weak/default credentials, including an administrator account (superadmin/md5('superadmin')) and users with trivially guessable passwords ('password', 'spidey'). Anyone with access to the source code can log in as the superadmin.
